source.title: Arkansas DSAS Office of Personnel Management Policy 52, 'Holidays and Birthday Leave' (eff. 2025-05-22), authority Ark. Code 1-5-101 to -104; Arkansas Secretary of State '2026 State Holidays' list (sos.arkansas.gov/uploads/holidays_2026.pdf)

renamedFederalHolidays.name: George Washington's Birthday and Daisy Gatson Bates Day

excludedConfederateHolidays.name: Jefferson Davis' Birthday (memorial day by proclamation; offices open)
Confederate Flag Day (observance by proclamation; offices open)

stateHolidays.name: Christmas Eve
stateHolidays.note: Statutory paid holiday (Ark. Code 1-5-101; Policy 52). Observed Thu Dec 24, 2026.

partialOrLocal.name: Employee birthday holiday
partialOrLocal.note: Policy 52: each employee is granted one holiday to observe his/her birthday. Counted by Arkansas among its 'eleven (11) paid holidays per year' (Ark. Code 1-5-101(c)).

partialOrLocal.name: Day after Thanksgiving (governor's proclamation)
partialOrLocal.note: Not in the statute. Governor Sanders closed state offices the Friday after Thanksgiving by proclamation in 2023 (Nov 24) and 2024 (Nov 29); I could not confirm a 2025 proclamation. A UA Little Rock 2026-27 memo lists Fri Nov 27, 2026 as holiday 'if granted by Governor's proclamation'. Discretionary; not counted.

partialOrLocal.name: Dec 26, 2025 closure (governor's proclamation)
partialOrLocal.note: Gov. Sanders closed state offices Fri Dec 26, 2025 by proclamation (KAIT, 2025-12-16). Ark. Code 1-5-103 allows additional closures by proclamation. One-off; not counted.

partialOrLocal.name: Juneteenth Independence Day
partialOrLocal.note: Memorial day observed by gubernatorial proclamation on the THIRD SATURDAY in June (not June 19); state offices not closed.

partialOrLocal.name: Memorial days by proclamation (Good Friday, Columbus Day Oct 12, Abraham Lincoln's Birthday Feb 12, etc.)
partialOrLocal.note: Per Encyclopedia of Arkansas: memorial days are observed by proclamation but are not paid legal holidays; offices stay open.
